events.title: Louis VIII becomes King of France on Philip Augustus's death
events.description: Philip II died at Mantes and his son Louis VIII succeeded him. In a reign of just three years Louis took Poitou from the English and led a royal crusade against the Cathars of the south.
events.html: Philip II died at Mantes and his son Louis VIII succeeded him. In a reign of just three years Louis took Poitou from the English and led a royal crusade against the Cathars of the south.

events.title: Parisians storm the Bastille
events.description: Crowds seeking gunpowder stormed the Bastille fortress, which held just seven prisoners. Its fall became the symbol of the French Revolution, and 14 July is France's national day.
events.html: Crowds seeking gunpowder stormed the Bastille fortress, which held just seven prisoners. Its fall became the symbol of the French Revolution, and 14 July is France's national day.

events.title: John Adams signs the Sedition Act
events.description: The Sedition Act made it a crime to publish 'false, scandalous and malicious' writing against the US government. It was used to prosecute Republican editors and helped Jefferson win the 1800 election.
events.html: The Sedition Act made it a crime to publish 'false, scandalous and malicious' writing against the US government. It was used to prosecute Republican editors and helped Jefferson win the 1800 election.

events.title: Edward Whymper's party makes the first ascent of the Matterhorn
events.description: A seven-man team led by Edward Whymper reached the summit of the Matterhorn. On the descent a rope broke and four men fell to their deaths, a tragedy that shocked Victorian Britain.
events.html: A seven-man team led by Edward Whymper reached the summit of the Matterhorn. On the descent a rope broke and four men fell to their deaths, a tragedy that shocked Victorian Britain.

events.title: Nazi Germany becomes a one-party state
events.description: The Law against the Formation of New Parties declared the Nazi Party the only legal party in Germany. Less than six months after Hitler became chancellor, organised political opposition had been outlawed.
events.html: The Law against the Formation of New Parties declared the Nazi Party the only legal party in Germany. Less than six months after Hitler became chancellor, organised political opposition had been outlawed.

events.title: Iraqi army officers overthrow the Hashemite monarchy
events.description: Officers led by Brigadier Abd al-Karim Qasim seized Baghdad and killed King Faisal II and members of the royal family. The coup ended the British-backed monarchy and made Iraq a republic.
